patch.objective: Recognize fluid volume overload during IV therapy -- rising blood pressure and respiratory rate, falling saturation, edema and crackles -- and act on it
secondaryObjectives: Assessing and responding to changes and trends in vital signs

sources.cite: McDonagh TA, et al. 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure. Eur Heart J 2021;42(36):3599-3726
sources.note: Relayed from the ADNRN case heart-failure-pulmonary-edema, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary text, acute heart failure section). Oxygen recommended for SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg; non-invasive positive pressure ventilation as soon as possible in respiratory distress (respiratory rate >25/min, SpO2 <90%); initial IV furosemide 1-2 times the daily oral dose taken before admission (20-40 mg if none); response checked by spot urine sodium after 2 or 6 h and/or hourly urine output, satisfactory if urine sodium >50-70 mEq/L at 2 h and/or urine output >100-150 mL/h in the first 6 h; IV vasodilators may be considered with SBP >110 mmHg; routine opiates not recommended.

sources.cite: Heidenreich PA, et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure. Circulation 2022;145:e895-e1032
sources.note: Relayed from the ADNRN case heart-failure-pulmonary-edema, not re-read for this band; its note: Read only through a secondary summary (The Hospitalist, 'How to treat heart failure: new updates', read 2026-11-11); the publisher pages refused the fetch. As summarized: patients admitted with significant fluid overload should be treated promptly with an IV loop diuretic; a patient on a home diuretic starts at about their total daily home dose given IV. The ACC's 2026-06-30 release on the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure says the next AHA/ACC management guideline is expected in late 2027, so the 2022 guideline is still current. No number in this case is taken from it.

sources.cite: Pfizer. Furosemide Injection, prescribing information (clinical pharmacology)
sources.note: Relayed from the ADNRN case heart-failure-pulmonary-edema, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary web page). After IV administration the onset of diuresis is within 5 minutes, the peak effect within the first half hour, and the diuretic effect lasts about 2 hours.
